profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC9 sits at 22210 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus; this record shares its address with CloudHQ LC10, also tracked separately in this dataset, since both derive from a single project address recorded by a third-party aggregator rather than individually distinct street addresses published by CloudHQ itself. CloudHQ's own current campus page places the site directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing it as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available, a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building; no third-party aggregator figure specific to LC9 alone was found either. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide and over 6,000 megawatts of further expansion potential, figures CloudHQ discloses on its own homepage alongside a stated 5.2-gigawatt global data center inventory.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC9 is a planned building within the LC Campus cluster in Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen data centers sharing a single project address on Loudoun County Parkway. The campus as a whole publishes 1,256 MW of total critical IT load and 756 MW available for new tenants. Individual building capacity for LC9 is not published by CloudHQ, though one third-party source lists 108 MW. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 108 MW would support roughly 2,700 racks, though this figure is not from the operator's specifications.

The LC Campus sits in Virginia's primary data center cluster and ranks 24th by published capacity among mapped facilities in the state. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities total, of which 23 publish megawatt figures, accounting for 1,375 MW of published critical IT load. The campus contributes most of the published capacity attributed to this single project address.

CloudHQ's certification status, compliance tier, renewable energy sourcing, and grid interconnection details are not published at the building level. The operator operates across twenty-three global campuses with more than 1,380 MW of contracted critical IT load, though whether LC9 is complete, funded, or under construction is not stated in available sources.
